**Visual Analysis:**

The test image shows a single mango leaf with:
- Predominantly green leaf surface
- Highly jagged/serrated margins with irregular notching
- Brown necrotic tissue specifically concentrated along the margins
- Gray stone/tile background

**Comparison with candidates:**
- **Bacterial_Canker** — The reference collage is an almost exact visual match: green leaves with deeply serrated necrotic margins on the same gray surface. The pattern and presentation are identical.
- **Cutting_Weevil** — Reference shows severely stripped leaves with barely any tissue remaining (just midribs with small fragments); test leaf retains full tissue. Ruled out.
- **Gall_Midge** — Reference shows raised bumps/galls on the leaf surface, not margin necrosis. Ruled out.
- **Anthracnose** — Shows yellowing/browning of entire leaf and tip lesions. Ruled out.
- **Powdery_Mildew** — White powdery spots on surface. Ruled out.
- **Sooty_Mould** — Black coating on surface. Ruled out.
- **Die_Back** — Fully dried/brown curled leaves. Ruled out.

The jagged margin necrosis with intact green leaf body is the hallmark of Bacterial_Canker in this dataset.
